title: VS Code Walkthrough
moduleObjectives: Explain what an IDE is and how VS Code combines an editor, a terminal, and other tools in one window
Navigate the VS Code UI, naming the activity bar, side bar, editor, panel, and status bar, and run commands from the command palette
Open the integrated terminal and distinguish typing into the terminal from typing into the editor
Install, disable, and uninstall extensions from the marketplace, verifying the publisher before installing
Install the Docker extension and explain why its sidebar is empty before Docker itself is installed
Connect VS Code to WSL on Windows and open a folder in the Linux home directory
Connect VS Code to a remote machine over SSH, open a remote folder, and verify the terminal runs on the remote

lessons.title: What is an IDE?
lessons.objective: Install VS Code and explain the difference between an editor, a terminal, and an IDE.

lessons.title: VS Code UI Tour
lessons.objective: Identify the activity bar, side bar, editor, panel, and status bar, and use the command palette (`Ctrl+Shift+P`) to toggle the terminal and change the editor font size.

lessons.title: The Integrated Terminal
lessons.objective: Open the integrated terminal, run `echo` commands at the prompt, and distinguish typing into the terminal from typing into the editor.

lessons.title: Extensions Overview
lessons.objective: Install the Python extension by Microsoft from the marketplace, verify its publisher first, and describe when to use Install, Disable, and Uninstall.

lessons.title: The Docker Extension
lessons.objective: Install the Docker extension by Microsoft, locate its whale icon and sidebar sections, and explain why the sidebar shows 'Failed to connect' before Docker is installed.

lessons.title: Connecting to WSL
lessons.objective: Connect VS Code to WSL using the WSL extension, open a folder in the Linux home directory, and verify the terminal is Linux by running `uname -a`.

lessons.title: Connecting over SSH
lessons.objective: Connect VS Code to an instructor-provided remote host with the Remote - SSH extension, open a remote folder, and confirm the session by running `hostname` and `whoami`.

lessons.title: Final Checkpoint
lessons.objective: Demonstrate unaided use of VS Code by toggling the terminal from the command palette, installing an extension, connecting to WSL or SSH, and capturing a screenshot showing the green remote indicator with `whoami` and `pwd` output.

quiz.question: According to the lessons, what makes VS Code an IDE rather than just an editor?
options: It requires you to sign in to a Microsoft account before use
It can only be used for writing code, not plain text
It combines an editor, a terminal, and other development tools in one window
It includes a built-in AI assistant out of the box
quiz.feedback: An IDE (Integrated Development Environment) bolts an editor, a terminal, and other tools together in one window so you don't have to switch between separate programs.

quiz.question: Which keyboard shortcut opens the VS Code command palette?
options: `Ctrl+Shift+P`
`Ctrl+,`
`Ctrl+Shift+X`
Ctrl+backtick
quiz.feedback: `Ctrl+Shift+P` (Cmd+Shift+P on Mac) opens the command palette, from which any VS Code command can be run by name.

quiz.question: In the VS Code window, what important information appears in the bottom-left section of the status bar?
options: The current file's word count
The list of installed extensions
The editor font size setting
Where VS Code is connected to, such as a WSL or SSH indicator
quiz.feedback: The bottom-left of the status bar shows what environment VS Code is connected to, which is where the green 'WSL: Ubuntu' or 'SSH: hostname' indicator appears.

quiz.question: You type `echo hello` into the big middle area of the VS Code window and nothing runs. What went wrong?
options: The command needs quotes around the word hello
You typed into the editor, which stores text in a file, instead of the terminal, which runs commands
The integrated terminal only works after Docker is installed
VS Code requires commands to be run from the command palette
quiz.feedback: The editor stores what you type into a file and never runs it; commands must be typed at the prompt in the terminal panel at the bottom.

quiz.question: Before clicking Install on an extension in the marketplace, what should you always check?
options: That the extension was updated within the last week
That the extension is smaller than 100 MB
The publisher shown under the extension name, since multiple extensions can share the same name
That the extension has screenshots on its details page
quiz.feedback: There are sometimes multiple extensions with the same name (like Python), so you must verify the publisher, such as Microsoft's `ms-python`, before installing.

quiz.question: After installing the Docker extension, its sidebar shows 'Failed to connect' or empty sections. Why?
options: The extension was published by the wrong publisher and must be reinstalled
Docker itself is not installed yet; that happens in Module 02, so the extension has nothing to talk to
The sidebar only populates when VS Code is connected over SSH
The whale icon must be clicked twice to start the Docker service
quiz.feedback: The extension is working correctly; Docker isn't installed until Module 02, so the sidebar has nothing to connect to and the empty state is expected.

quiz.question: What is the correct way to install WSL if `wsl --status` shows it is not installed?
options: Run `wsl --install` in PowerShell as administrator, then reboot the computer
Install the WSL extension in VS Code, which installs WSL automatically
Run `wsl --status --install` in the VS Code integrated terminal
Download WSL from code.visualstudio.com and run the installer
quiz.feedback: WSL is installed by running `wsl --install` in an administrator PowerShell, and the installation requires a reboot before Ubuntu finishes setting up.

quiz.question: After connecting VS Code to WSL, which command confirms your integrated terminal is really running Linux?
options: `echo hello`, which prints hello back
`wsl --status`, which prints the default distribution
`pwd`, which prints the current folder
`uname -a`, whose output mentions Linux
quiz.feedback: The lesson has you run `uname -a` and check that the output mentions 'Linux' as proof that the terminal is inside WSL.

quiz.question: When first connecting to a new SSH host, VS Code shows 'The authenticity of host ... can't be established. Are you sure you want to continue connecting (yes/no/[fingerprint])?' What must you do?
options: Type `yes` and press Enter, because pressing Enter alone does nothing
Press Enter to accept the default answer
Type the remote machine's password
Close the prompt and reconnect from the command palette
quiz.feedback: The prompt has no default answer, so you must explicitly type `yes` and press Enter; pressing Enter by itself does nothing.

quiz.question: On Mac or Linux, why do you run `chmod 600` on your SSH key file before connecting?
options: It converts the key into a format VS Code can read
It registers the key with the Remote - SSH extension
SSH refuses to use keys that anyone else can read, so the permissions must be locked down
It encrypts the key with your login password
quiz.feedback: `chmod 600` locks down the key file's permissions so only you can read it, which SSH requires before it will accept the key.
